question.passageWithMarkers: The structure of glass is, frankly, a bit of a mess. Clear and perfect as __(A) it__ might appear to our eyes, down at the molecular level, glass looks more like a random ball-pit of atoms. The technical term for this mess depends on who you're asking: for some scientists it is an "amorphous solid," for others a "supercooled liquid." In theory it's both liquid and solid, though, given the way it behaves, in practice it's really the latter. In fact, at room temperature glass never behaves as a liquid, even an imperceptibly viscous one, even over long periods of time (though it can "sweat" if you don't add enough lime to the mix). Those misshapen sheets of glass you sometimes see in old stained-glass windows, thicker at the bottom than the top, __(B) are__ generally not that way because the glass __(C) was slowly sunk__ over time. Unless the church has endured temperatures of more than 400˚C, the chances are they are uneven because that's the way they were blown and solidified in the first place. Flat glass was only developed in the nineteenth century and we had to wait until the middle of the twentieth century for truly flat, thin sheets of glass. The paradox is that, __(D) despite__ it being one of the very oldest human-made substances, scientists still struggle __(E) to comprehend__ why glass behaves the way it does. Glass seems to obey most molecular laws. As one glassmaker put it, glass is not a material; it's a state.

fatalIssues: (D)의 오류가 'why glass behaves the way it does'에서 주어 glass와 동사가 바로 인접해 있어, 원거리/절 간 구조 추적이 필요 없는 지나치게 국지적인 함정임
majorIssues: 오답 설명에서 'appear'를 '감각동사'로 지칭했는데 이는 국어 문법 용어상 look/feel/smell 류에 쓰는 표현으로, 연결동사(linking verb)로서의 appear와 혼동될 수 있음
(A)(B)(C)(E) 네 개의 정답 보기가 서로 다른 문법 포인트(도치, 수일치, 대명사, 대동사)를 산발적으로 다루어 하나의 정교한 함정 구조 없이 형식적 나열에 그침
난이도 표기는 INTERMEDIATE이나 실제 정답 판별은 매우 단순한 주어-동사 인접 구조로, 표기된 난이도와 실제 변별력이 불일치함
minorIssues: (C)의 'it' 지시대상이 지문 전체 주제인 glass로 상당히 넓은 범위에서 추론되어야 하나 설명이 이를 명확히 짚지 않음
strengths: 나머지 네 개 보기(A,B,C,E)는 각각 어법적으로 명확히 올바르며 근거가 원문과 일치함
정답 (D)의 correction과 explanation이 서로 모순 없이 일관되게 behaves로 수렴함
